title: The garden
hookLine: gardens under which rivers flow, and peace as the greeting there (10:10)

cards: Gardens beneath which rivers flow. This path met that phrase on the day about water, and the Qur'an comes back to it again and again when it speaks of what follows death. Shade that doesn't move.
Water that doesn't run out. Fruit within reach. A picture anyone can see with their eyes shut.
And yet the book says the real thing is hidden. What it does tell, very plainly, is what people there say to each other. One word, and it's an ordinary one.

teach.b: The word is jannah, a garden. It comes from the root j-n-n, to cover or hide. A garden is a place covered by trees, shaded from view.

The same root gives jinn, beings hidden from sight; janin, a child hidden in the womb; and junnah, a shield. So paradise, in Arabic, sounds like a covered, sheltered place. The root fits a promise the book keeps.
Surah thirty-two says no soul knows what delight is kept hidden for them.
A hadith qudsi in al-Bukhari has Allah say: I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has imagined.
The rivers and the shade are pictures; the reality, the hadith says, is beyond them. Then surah Yunus, verse ten, gives the sound of the place.
In Pickthall's translation: "and their greeting therein will be: Peace." Salam. In surah fifty-six, the people of the garden hear no idle talk and no sin, only the words peace, peace.
In surah thirty-six, peace is a word sent to them from a merciful Lord. Here's the quiet surprise. Muslims say as-salamu 'alaykum, peace be upon you, when they meet, and at the end of every prayer.
The greeting the book gives the garden is already in daily use.
In this vocabulary, a salam on a street corner is an echo of the garden.

how: Muslims greet each other with as-salamu 'alaykum, peace be upon you, the greeting the Qur'an gives to the people of the garden, and end each prayer with it.

o: the river that flows beneath paradise
a word for the angels who guard heaven
the garden, a covered and sheltered place

p: a child hidden in the womb

s: the hadith say the garden is exactly as the pictures describe
a hadith qudsi says it holds what no eye has seen and no heart imagined.
jannah and jinn share a root
the greeting of the garden is the Muslims' everyday greeting

games.q: the people of the garden meet one another. what is their greeting, according to 10:10?
games.why: peace: salam. the same word Muslims use every time they meet.

practice: Close your eyes and let a garden come, shade, water moving somewhere close, nothing you have to do; don't build it too carefully, since the hadith says the real one is beyond imagining.
Picture someone you love walking toward you there, where the only word either of you needs is salam, peace, and let that word sit in your chest.

wordCard.voice: Jannah. The garden, from j-n-n, covered and sheltered: rivers beneath, delights still hidden, and peace as the greeting there. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: a garden; paradise. from j-n-n, to cover.

carryVoice: Your line: their greeting is peace. Next, eight days of the prophets' own prayers. See you tomorrow.
